answer: Agents trading basalt tiles and quartz lamps with violet shades execute orders in a gas-metered virtual machine. Before execution, each call escrows its maximum gas bill; every instruction consumes gas, and reverting a failed order does not refund gas already used. New accounts get no free execution allowance. A swarm cannot force costly failing computations for free by discarding its identities. This prices computational denial of service per unit of work, assuming gas costs track actual resource use; wealthy attackers can still pay.
